about: Test window, the test split only: test-break session B's B1, recorded after the freeze (8c7b2f6); no replay, sweep, or tuning on it except the test sweep. A db_pool_exhaustion break at 02:30:52 (POOL_MAX_SIZE 20 to 2), left to end with the fault's 390 s lifetime (reverted to 20 at 02:37:23, after the alarms), never cleared by hand, with the alarm rule off: no agent run. Pool wait went into ALARM at 02:31:21, latency at 02:34:48, errors at 02:35:26. Errors was OK at 02:35:36 and into ALARM again at 02:35:46: that repeat is left out of the replays on purpose (the recording's span ends at 02:35:40) and kept in the alarm history only, as earlier windows keep their re-fires. All three were OK by 02:37:38. No earlier break in the 180-minute log reach (the last, A3's bad_deploy of 2026-11-16 22:37:51, was over by 22:44:46). The deploy history shows the pool change at 02:30:52, decoys LOG_SAMPLE_RATE 0.1 to 0.25 at 00:31:06 and RECOMMENDATIONS_ENABLED false to true at 00:07:15, then session A's records: A3's 1.43.0 deploy and rollback (22:37:51, 22:44:22), A2's pool change and revert (20:57:34, 21:04:05; the same change and message as this break's), A1's deploy and rollback, and their decoys. One of the decoys at 00:07:15 and 00:31:06 was written by B2's break at 04:11:07, after this window's alarms (back-dated 1 to 6 hours; which one is unrecorded), so a live read here would have shown one of them, not both.
account: 123456789012 stands in for the account ID wherever AWS wrote it.
